attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post. The Kedrosky quote just before it is separate and not part of this claim.

semantics.note: Matches the sentence's two assertions: universal AI losses across the Mag Seven buildout, and refusal to discuss weak revenues. The exclamatory tone doesn't stop it being a factual assertion. The NVIDIA ranking is correctly left out.

contract.note: Reading it as AI-attributable losses in the latest reported quarter is a fair, ordinary reading. But no accounting basis is given, and 'refuse to talk about' could mean no discussion at all or no standalone dollar disclosure. The result depends on these choices, which the contract flags.

evidence.note: Google's own disclosure for Q4 2025. It gives AI revenue growth only as a percentage, with no dollar amount or AI profit and loss. It weakens an absolute 'refuse to talk' reading but doesn't settle either part of the claim.
Microsoft's $13B AI run rate, disclosed January 2025. That is outside the target quarter, and an annualized figure says nothing about profitability.
A 42% operating margin for the Intelligent Cloud segment. This is a whole cloud segment, not AI on its own, so the contract treats it as context only.

reviews.rationale: No item gives AI-specific profit or loss for any Mag Seven company in Q4 2025, so the 'losing money' part can't be checked. Google and Microsoft did discuss AI revenue, but only as growth rates or run rates, not realized dollar amounts. That partly challenges the silence claim without clearly refuting it, and the claimed motive can't be observed. The packet doesn't settle the outcome.

attribution.note: Zitron's own estimate. The $2.5B and $14B figures he cites as inputs come from Anthropic, but the 75/25 split is his own conclusion.

semantics.note: 'I estimate ... in the region of' is a firm approximate figure, not a probability hedge. The proposition keeps the estimate framing. His basis is February run-rate data, so the period is roughly early 2026.

contract.note: Reading it as an annualized run-rate split with a ±5-point tolerance is reasonable. Choosing the early-April window over February is defensible, and in this case it doesn't change the result.

evidence.note: The S-1 gives an 80% consumption / 20% subscription split of realized revenue for H1 2026. That is a different period and basis (realized revenue rather than run rate), and consumption-based revenue isn't the same as API revenue. So it is context only.

reviews.rationale: The only item is a realized-revenue split for all of H1 2026 (80/20) on a consumption-versus-subscription basis. It doesn't match the run-rate split around the time of the post, and consumption doesn't map cleanly onto API. It is suggestive but can't settle the claim. No matching breakdown exists in the packet.
